rows.requirement: Title is FrackingAsteroids; genre is Arcade / Resource Management
Platform target is web for desktop and mobile browsers
Tech stack is Next.js, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, and Upstash Redis
Art style is voxel-style 3D
Elevator pitch: blast asteroids, collect fragments, scrap resources, reinvest in upgrading blaster, collector, and storage
Win condition: reach maximum upgrade tier across all three systems (blaster, collector, storage)
Core loop is BLAST then COLLECT then SCRAP then UPGRADE, repeating
Blast: shoot asteroids with the blaster to break them into fragments
Collect: fly through or attract fragments with the collector beam
Scrap: fragments auto-convert to scrap (currency) in the cargo hold
Upgrade: spend scrap to improve blaster, collector, or storage capacity
Blaster is a short-range mining tool with amber energy pulses that chip away at asteroids, forcing the player to fly close to their claim
Blaster tier 1: 1/sec fire rate, 200 u/s projectile speed (base), 1 damage, no spread
Blaster tier 2: 2/sec fire rate, 250 u/s (+25%), 1 damage, no spread
Blaster tier 3: 3/sec fire rate, 300 u/s (+50%), 2 damage, no spread
Blaster tier 4: 4/sec fire rate, 350 u/s (+75%), 2 damage, dual spread (plus or minus 8 degrees)
Blaster tier 5: 5/sec fire rate, 400 u/s (+100%), 3 damage, triple spread (0, plus or minus 10 degrees)
Projectile base speed is 200 units/sec, exceeding ship cruise speed (~56 u/s) so bolts outrun the ship
Projectile lifetime is 1.5 seconds (~300 unit max range, shorter effective mining range)
Projectile visual is a 2 to 3 voxel elongated amber pulse with color 0xFFAA00
Projectile collision uses a circle-circle radius check against asteroids
Collector tier 1: small range, slow pull speed, no auto-collect
Collector tier 2: medium range, medium pull speed, no auto-collect
Collector tier 3: large range, fast pull speed, no auto-collect
Collector tier 4: XL range, fast pull speed, auto-collects nearby fragments
Collector tier 5: XXL range, instant pull speed, auto-collects all fragments on screen
Storage tier 1: capacity 50, scrap bonus 0%
Storage tier 2: capacity 125, scrap bonus 10%
Storage tier 3: capacity 250, scrap bonus 20%
Storage tier 4: capacity 500, scrap bonus 35%
Storage tier 5: capacity 1000, scrap bonus 50%
Player ship has 100 HP
HP is lost when the ship is hit by enemy projectiles
HP is restored to full when passing through the gas station (drive-through repair)
HP is persisted across saves
Common asteroid: large size, brown / blue crystal palette, 15 HP
Dense asteroid: medium size, gray-purple / violet palette, 14 HP
Precious asteroid: small size, gold / yellow accent palette, 6 HP
Comet asteroid: varies in size, blue-teal / cyan palette, 10 HP
Crystalline asteroid: varies in size, deep purple / magenta palette, 30 HP, immune to the standard blaster and requires a Lazer to mine
Asteroids drift across the field at varying speeds and angles
Asteroids are spawned in a ring around the gas station after the tutorial
Asteroids are voxel models with seeded shapes for visual variety
Lazer is a sustained beam mining tool: continuous solid beam while the fire button is held, applying instant line-of-sight damage with no projectile travel time
Lazer is purchased at the Trade Station for 200 scrap
Lazer deals 1.5x damage multiplier to all asteroid types
Lazer beam color is cyan 0x00CCFF with a bright core 0x88EEFF
Lazer is required to mine crystalline asteroids
Lazer beam range is 120 world units, rendered as a solid glowing cyan line from ship to first asteroid hit or max range
Lazer DPS is 5x base tier damage per second, applied continuously every frame
Lazer heat builds at 1.0 heat/sec while firing; meter under the ship fills cyan to orange as heat rises
Lazer max heat is 1.5 seconds of sustained fire; at max heat it overheats with a forced stop, meter turns red and drains over the cooldown
Lazer overheat cooldown is 1.5 seconds, after which heat resets to 0 and the lazer is ready again
Lazer passively dissipates heat at 0.5/sec when not firing and not overheated, enabling burst-fire strategies
Players switch between the Blaster and Lazer via a HUD dropdown
A tutorial popup appears each time the player deflects off crystalline with the blaster, freezing the game until any tap on screen dismisses it
Desktop: WASD or arrow keys move the ship (twin-stick: movement independent of aim)
Desktop: mouse cursor aims the ship (ship rotates to face cursor)
Desktop: mouse click fires the blaster toward the cursor
Desktop: right-click held, or E or Space held, activates the collector
Desktop: Space pauses (revealing the Feedback FAB)
Mobile: left thumb virtual joystick (floating anchor, left half of screen) moves the ship
Mobile: right thumb firing joystick (floating anchor, right half) sets projectile direction by stick angle; blaster cooldown / lazer heat gate actual shots
Mobile: visible circular blue collect button on bottom-right, held to activate the metal attractor
Mobile: pause button in the HUD
Ship rotation is decoupled from movement: always faces the aim target, and falls back to movement direction when no aim target is active
Virtual joystick uses a fixed dead zone of 10px to prevent drift
Visual style: voxel art, chunky colorful 3D blocks
Perspective camera presents a top-down view of the asteroid field

Scene color palette: deep navy/black space background with subtle star particles, earthy asteroids with gold/crystal highlights, metallic blue-gray ship with glowing engine trails, bright glowing fragments matching asteroid type, green and blue neon HUD against dark overlays
Camera is a fixed top-down view that follows the ship with smooth lerp
Gas station is located north of the starting area
Gas station provides drive-through repair: restores HP to full when passing close
Gas station trade menu sells materials for scrap and buys upgrades

Prologue starts with a fully upgraded ship (Blaster Mk5, Collector Mk5, Storage Mk5, Lazer unlocked), visually larger with detachable module add-ons (weapon turrets, collector scoop, cargo pods, lazer emitter) and gold accents
Prologue auto-fire targets the nearest asteroid/enemy automatically
Prologue auto-mine: the lazer beam shreds asteroids including moon-sized rocks (size 0, ~30 world units)
Prologue auto-collect: magnet collector with 40-unit range vacuums all debris
Prologue phase 1 Mining: lazer annihilates a dense field of 30 asteroids plus 3 moon-size rocks
Prologue phase 2 Combat: triple-fire blaster destroys a 6-ship enemy fleet
Prologue phase 3 Speed: boosted max speed (180 u/s) showcase
Prologue phase 4 The Arbiter: a massive AI construct (~20x20 world units) warps in and freezes the ship
Prologue phase 5 Strip: the Arbiter removes modules one by one (turrets, scoop, cargo, lazer)
Prologue phase 6 Fade: 'Systems offline.' then 'Rebooting...' then player respawns with a tier-1 ship
The Arbiter is an all-powerful AI enforcing belt balance; delivers three lines: 'You have grown too powerful, fracker.', 'The belt was not built for one to dominate.', 'I am restoring balance.'
After the prologue, the existing tutorial begins with the player motivated to rebuild
A SKIP INTRO button is available at any time during the prologue
Loading a saved game skips the prologue entirely
Moon asteroids are size 0, prologue-only, with voxel size 3.0 and collision radius 16
Moon asteroid HP ranges from 25 (precious) to 80 (crystalline)
Moon asteroids use 5 voxel layers for imposing depth
Ship schema has fields x, y, rotation, velocityX, velocityY
Upgrades schema has fields blaster (number), collector (number), storage (number)
Cargo schema has fields scrap, fragments, silver, gold, capacity
GameState schema has fields ship, upgrades, cargo, hp, timestamp
Game state lives in the Three.js render loop at 60fps
React state for UI/HUD is managed via the useGameState hook
Persistence is provided via the useGamePersistence hook backed by Upstash Redis
Auto-save triggers on resource collection, selling, buying, and station repair
A headless GameSimulation mirrors scene.ts orchestration for integration testing
GET /api/game/[id] loads saved game state
PUT /api/game/[id] saves game state
GET /api/health returns a health check
GET /api/version returns the current build version
POST /api/feedback submits player feedback
Scrap counter is in the top-left, showing the current scrap amount
Cargo bar is in the top-left below scrap, showing fragments/capacity
Upgrade indicators are in the top-right, showing the current tier for each system
Recharge meter is a small horizontal bar below the ship showing blaster cooldown progress
Aim reticle: a red dashed semi-transparent line from the ship center in aim direction extending to screen edge or stopping at the first asteroid/enemy intersection
Aim reticle target circle marks where shots land: centered on the screen-edge endpoint when clear, or snapped onto and sized to the intersected object
Aim reticle is hidden during the scripted prologue
Health bar is shown when HP is below max
Pause button is in the top-right corner (mobile uses a larger touch target)
Start screen is a full-screen menu shown on app launch with title 'FRACKING ASTEROIDS' and a tagline
New Game button opens a save slot picker with 3 slots
Load Game button opens a save slot picker with 3 slots
Each save slot shows its last-save timestamp
Save slot summaries are stored in localStorage for instant display
Pause overlay darkens the game canvas
Pause overlay shows 'PAUSED' text centered
Pause overlay shows a Resume button
Pause overlay reveals the Feedback FAB (floating action button, bottom-right)
All game objects are built from voxel-style geometry
Ship is a ~8x8x4 voxel block ship with engine glow
Asteroids are irregular voxel clusters, procedurally varied per type
Fragments are small 1 to 2 voxel glowing cubes
Projectiles are bright amber elongated voxel pulses (mining laser bolts)
Background is a particle-based star field
Screen shake is trauma-based: damage adds trauma (0 to 1), quadratic falloff for intensity, camera offset oscillates at 25 Hz, decays at 4.0/sec, triggered when hit by enemy projectiles
Engine trail emits glowing orange/red particles from the ship rear, with emission rate and brightness scaling with ship speed, fading and shrinking over 0.4 seconds
Background twinkling stars: 200 colored points with per-star brightness oscillation
Background nebula swirls: 5 large semi-transparent glowing clouds with additive blending
Background black hole: dark core with 4 spinning accretion rings (orange/red gradient)
All background layers parallax at different rates for depth
Explosion effect plays when asteroids/enemies are hit

Color palette: space #0a0a1a to #111133 gradient; mining laser #FFAA00 amber and #FFDD44 bright core; HUD #00FF88 green, #00AAFF blue, #FF4444 red, #FFAA00 amber; engine trail #FF6600/#FF4400/#FF8800/#FFAA00; nebulae #220044/#001133/#110022; black hole rings #FF4400/#FF8800/#FFAA00/#FF6600
All audio is procedurally synthesized using the Web Audio API with no external audio files

Background music is a four-layer procedural soundtrack: layer 0 deep bass drone (always playing), layer 1 pad chords (fade in at low intensity), layer 2 arpeggiated melody (fade in during moderate activity), layer 3 percussion pulse (fade in during combat)
Music intensity lerps smoothly between peaceful (0.15) and combat (0.8)
SFX laser fire: short chirpy zap (bandpass-filtered square wave)
SFX explosion: low boom with noise burst when asteroids/enemies are hit
SFX player hit: sharp impact with distortion crack
SFX engine thrust: filtered noise loop, volume/frequency scale with ship speed
SFX collector hum: low sawtooth drone when the magnet is active
SFX collection pling: metallic ping on pickup
M1 Skeleton complete: project setup, build pipeline, deploy to Vercel
M2 Flight complete: ship rendering and movement (desktop plus mobile)
M3 Mining complete: blaster firing, asteroid collision, debris and metal spawning
M4 Economy complete: metal collection, scrap conversion, trade menu at station
M5 Upgrades complete: upgrade purchasing at station, tier progression
M6 Tutorial complete: guided onboarding with tutorial state machine
M7 Asteroid Field complete: multiple asteroid types/sizes spawned after tutorial
M8 Persistence complete: auto-save on game events, KV backend storage
M9 Polish complete: background music, SFX, particles, screen shake, background effects
M10 Lazer & Crystalline complete: crystalline asteroid type, Lazer mining tool, HUD tool switcher, trade station purchase
M11 Prologue complete: maxed ship intro with auto-fire/mine/collect, The Arbiter antagonist, module strip, prologue-to-tutorial transition
